title: Passive-to-Active Vocabulary Activation
dataSources: Lessons (`lesson:complete`), vocab reviews (`vocab:review`), immersion (`immersion:log`), speaking practice (`speaking:session`).
app: Language-learning telemetry — Duolingo / Babbel lesson exports, Anki spaced-repetition review logs, immersion trackers, and speaking-practice logs — streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=vocab:review
| stats dc(eval(if(context="immersion",term,null()))) as passive_terms, dc(eval(if(context="speaking",term,null()))) as active_terms by language
| eval activation_pct=round(100*active_terms/passive_terms,1)
| sort - activation_pct
description: Compares how much vocabulary you only recognize passively versus how much you actively use in speaking.
value: Activation is the bridge between study and fluency; this ratio makes the passive-active gap concrete.
implementation: Tag review terms by usage context and compare distinct passive versus active terms by language.
visualization: Table of languages with passive-to-active activation percentage.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how many words you can actually use out loud instead of only recognizing them when you see them.
